page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a single thread per core, backed by 256 GB of system memory, which translates to an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The server includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional memory performance, with large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 405.8 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 184.15 GB/sec, both placing in the top tier. Multi-core performance is also strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21506.0 and high throughput in database operations. However, the server exhibits limitations in specific workloads; for instance, large-model LLM prompt processing and small-model LLM text generation fall into the lower performance tiers.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and integrated high-speed NVMe SSD storage, the r8gd.8xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads without requiring external storage attachments. It is highly suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server utilizing 32 dedicated ARM64 physical cores from the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 family. Operating at 2.8 GHz, the instance provides 256 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. It includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 15 Gbps baseline network speed. Benchmark results place its large-block memory read and write bandwidth in the top tier, alongside exceptional database operation performance. While multi-core processing and memory throughput are highly competitive, the server shows weaker performance in certain LLM inference tasks. This hardware profile makes the r8gd.8xlarge highly efficient for memory-intensive databases, Redis deployments, and high-throughput web serving.
